Title: Stored XSS in Web UI Job Lists/Details via Unescaped Job Class Names
Analysis: The Sidekiq Web UI displays executing/pending/dead/retrying/scheduled jobs on several pages (such as `/busy`, `/morgue`, `/retries`, `/scheduled`, and individual job info pages). The job's class name (retrieved by calling `job.display_class` or `entry.display_class`) is fetched directly from the Redis job payload (specifically the `'class'` attribute or derived display wrapper). These values are rendered directly into the HTML body using ERB's unescaped `<%= ... %>` tags, without performing HTML entity encoding or escaping. An attacker who has access to queue a job or can inject/control a job payload (for instance, via a compromised or external microservice, or any interface that enqueues work to Redis) can construct a payload where the class name is a malicious HTML/JavaScript string. When an administrator or dashboard user views any of the job status/list views, the payload executes. This affects the following files: 1. `web/views/_job_info.erb` (line 17): `<%= job.display_class %>` 2. `web/views/busy.erb` (line 138): `<%= job.display_class %>` 3. `web/views/morgue.erb` (line 42): `<%= entry.display_class %>` 4. `web/views/retries.erb` (line 44): `<%= entry.display_class %>` 5. `web/views/scheduled.erb` (line 41): `<%= entry.display_class %>` ### Conceptual Exploit Payload: Push a job payload to Redis with a malicious `class` attribute: `{ "class": "", "args": [] }` When the `/busy` or `/morgue` page is loaded, the unescaped script tag is injected into the table, leading to stored XSS: ```html ... ```

Title: Stored XSS in Web UI Job Metrics via Unescaped Job Class Names
Analysis: The Sidekiq Web UI displays job metrics under the `/metrics` endpoint. The job class names (represented by the local variable `kls`) are dynamically populated from the keys in the Redis hash keys of metric data. This values are split to retrieve the class name and then rendered directly into the HTML body without sanitization or HTML entity encoding. Specifically, in `web/views/metrics.erb` on lines 65, 70, and 73, the unescaped `kls` is output inside tag attributes (such as `id` and `value`) and directly as inner text of an `` tag, allowing an attacker who can queue jobs with arbitrary class names to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). ### Conceptual Exploit Payload: Queue/register job with a malicious class name containing HTML markup: `">` When the metrics page is loaded, the metric entry is retrieved and rendered into the templates: ```html " ... value="...">" /> ?period=">"> ``` This breaks out of attributes and executes arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the user viewing the dashboard.
Snippet: <% id = "metrics-swatch-#{kls}" %> /> <%= kls %>
